title: Certified stationary distribution and hitting statistic numerics

items.title: Finite column-stochastic matrices and probability vectors
items.statement: Define the column-stochastic convention for finite Markov matrices, column probability vectors, and the transpose relation to the published row-transition convention.

items.title: Finite-step escape from a transient substochastic block
items.statement: For a finite row-substochastic block in which every state has a positive path to a row with positive escape probability, construct L≤n and ε>0 such that T^L 1≤(1−ε)1; conclude spectral radius strictly below one.

items.statement: A finite nonnegative column-stochastic matrix preserves coordinate sums and is nonexpansive in the vector ℓ1 norm.

items.title: Transient hitting, mean exit, and residual bounds
items.statement: For a finite row-substochastic transient block satisfying the finite-step escape hypothesis, prove (I−T)^{-1}=ΣT^k≥0, bound its induced infinity norm by L/ε, identify hitting and mean exit statistics, and bound solve error from the residual.

items.statement: For a finite irreducible row-stochastic matrix, prove existence of a positive invariant probability and show every real invariant row vector is its scalar multiple.

items.statement: For a finite column-stochastic P, identify the induced ℓ1 norm of P on the zero-sum subspace with half the maximum pairwise column distance and with one minus the minimum column overlap.

items.title: Correctness of finite Markov closed-class decomposition
items.statement: For an admissible exact finite column-stochastic matrix, the graph procedure terminates and returns exactly the strongly connected components and closed classes of its positive-transition graph. Every state outside the closed classes has a positive path to a closed class; its transient block therefore satisfies the finite-step escape hypothesis.

sources.locator: §11.2, Theorem 11.3 and canonical form, printed pp. 416–420; finite paths from nonabsorbing states to recurrent absorbing classes are used in the local graph classification proof.

items.title: Correct and certify a finite-chain stationary candidate
items.statement: For exact rational P and a rational raw vector y, clip and normalize its positive part, compute the correction distance, residual, and column-overlap coefficient of P^m, and return a certified bound or certificate-unavailable.

items.statement: For a finite chain, classify all stationary laws as convex combinations of the unique laws on closed classes and prove that the Cesàro averages from an initial law converge to the mixture whose weights are its class-hitting probabilities.
